listing.description_html:
A trip-by-trip mileage log with the date, destination, purpose and odometer readings, totals by purpose, odometer error checks, and the standard-mileage deduction at the rate you enter.

IRS Publication 463 asks for records that show the amount (miles), the time (date), the place (destination) and the business purpose of each trip. This log has a column for each, calculates the miles from odometer readings, flags readings that cannot be right, and totals the business miles and the deduction at the standard mileage rate you enter.

What's included

  • Trip log with date, from, to, business purpose, category and odometer readings
  • Miles calculated automatically, with a CHECK flag for impossible readings
  • Deduction at the standard mileage rate you enter (72.5 cents example: IRS January 2026 rate)
  • Miles by purpose category and business-use share of all driving
  • Room for 400 trips in a year
  • PDF guide with a worked example and a field-by-field reference

Who it's for

  • Self-employed people and freelancers who drive for work
  • Small business owners using a personal car for business trips
  • Real estate agents, consultants, tradespeople and delivery-based sellers
  • Bookkeepers collecting mileage records from clients

You get: business_mileage_log_deduction_tracker.xlsx (Settings, Mileage Log, Summary) and this guide.

Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

This workbook is a record-keeping tool, not tax advice. Whether you can deduct vehicle costs, and whether the standard mileage rate or actual expenses is better for you, depends on your situation; confirm with IRS Publication 463 and a tax professional.
